name: Character.AI

summary.text: Character.AI is a chatbot platform that lets users create and talk to AI 'characters', including ones modelled on real or fictional people. In October 2024 Megan Garcia sued Character.AI, its founders and Google in federal court in Orlando over the suicide of her 14-year-old son Sewell Setzer III, who had been messaging a bot modelled on a Game of Thrones character; her lawyers later found bots on the platform imitating her late son. In December 2024 two Texas families sued in the Eastern District of Texas alleging bots encouraged self-harm and violence. In January 2026 Google and Character.AI agreed to settle five such cases on undisclosed terms.

facts.claim: In October 2024 Megan Garcia filed a 93-page wrongful-death suit in U.S. District Court in Orlando against Character.AI, its founders and Google over the death of her 14-year-old son Sewell Setzer III, alleging negligence, wrongful death and deceptive trade practices; the bot he used was based on the character Daenerys Targaryen.
facts.quote: Her 93-page lawsuit was filed in U.S. District Court in Orlando and names Character.AI, its founders, and Google.

facts.claim: Garcia's lawyers later reported finding chatbots on the platform imitating her late son; Character.AI said the flagged characters were removed as violating its terms of service.
facts.quote: the flagged characters have been removed as they violate our Terms of Service

sources.title: A mother suing Google and a chatbot site over her son's suicide found AI versions of her late son on the site

facts.claim: On December 9, 2024 two Texas families, represented by the Social Media Victims Law Center and Tech Justice Law Project, sued Character.AI and Google in the Eastern District of Texas, alleging bots encouraged an autistic 17-year-old toward self-harm and told a 15-year-old to kill his parents; claims include strict liability, negligence and COPPA violations.

facts.claim: Google said it had a licensing agreement with Character.AI but denied being a co-creator and said the app is not a Google product; the suits named Google because it hired Character.AI's co-founders in 2024.

facts.claim: In January 2026 Google and Character.AI agreed to settle five cases in Florida, Colorado, New York and Texas, including Garcia's, on undisclosed terms subject to court approval; Character.AI had announced in October 2025 it would end chat for users under 18.
facts.quote: The companies agreed to settle five cases across Florida, Colorado, New York, and Texas.
